house/ervin-forecast-2026-11-02.json.scope: All 435 districts with current 2026 voting boundaries where changed. 433 comparable congressional D/R numerical scenarios; AK ranked-choice and CA-06 independent contest show only sourced Cook ratings. The 173 new-map presidential allocations are reconstructed estimates and have extra uncertainty, not certified 2026 election counts.

method.formula: House D−R estimate = dated national generic House polling + past-only selected alpha × [0.75 × (2024 district presidential D−R − national 2024 D−R) + 0.25 × (2020 district presidential D−R − national 2020 D−R)], blended only with candidate-compatible House district surveys. Same office, same formula scored on 2018/2022, chronological 2024 holdout. No Senate/Governor historical errors.

research/governor-same-office-2014-2024..sourcesScope: 57 distinct sourced 2018–24 governor race-year comparisons, plus linked 2018/2022 Wikipedia history; an election with multiple poll aggregates is represented by at most one selected comparison.
research/governor-same-office-2014-2024..signConvention: Democratic share minus Republican share; third parties and undecided are not reassigned. Poll errors = published D–R polling margin minus actual D–R result.
research/governor-same-office-2014-2024..qualityWarning: Reconstructed 270toWin three-poll means are not published official aggregates; single polls (including a 41-day-old NE partisan survey) are weaker and shrunk; Alaska uses first-choice multi-candidate margins consistently, NOT final-round RCV outcomes. Results alone never yield a polling error. This archive does not make a one-cycle correction a held-out historical backtest; first-cycle historical rows are unscorable in past-only validation.

editorial.headline: A Blue House. A Senate Cliffhanger.
editorial.dek: The 144,000-scenario Ervin Model centers on roughly 249 Democratic House seats, 50 Democratic-aligned Senate seats, and 27 Democratic governorships. Republicans have the narrower but meaningful Senate-control edge; simulations are sensitivity tests, not calibrated probabilities.
